## Set-up
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(arcgis)
library(mapview)
library(janitor)
library(treemapify)
library(sysfonts)
library(showtext)

# colors 
soe_colors <- c(
  red    = "#DD5A54",
  blush  = "#EDBFB2",
  orange = "#EC940C",
  blue   = "#608ED8",
  olive  = "#737F2E",
  forest = "#283523"
)
soe_palette <- unname(soe_colors)

## add fonts
font_add_google("Fraunces", "Fraunces")
font_add_google("Manrope", "Manrope")
showtext_auto()
showtext_opts(dpi = 300)

# ggplot theme
theme_soe <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Manrope") +
    theme(
      text             = element_text(color = soe_colors["forest"]),
      plot.title       = element_text(family = "Fraunces", face = "bold",
                                      size = rel(1.4)),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(face = "italic", size = rel(1.1)),
      axis.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border     = element_rect(color = soe_colors["forest"],
                                      fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
      strip.background = element_rect(color = soe_colors["forest"],
                                      fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
      strip.text       = element_text(family = "Fraunces", face = "bold",
                                      color = soe_colors["forest"])
    )
}
theme_set(theme_soe())
```

## Read in Priority Natural Communities Core
Data accessed from [BioMap Feature Layer](https://wellesley.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=d5f44922e5e446b3a3bd0a32dd04a498#overview)
```{r}
furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/BioMap_CoreHabitatComponents/FeatureServer/1"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
pncc <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> mutate(layer = "pncc")


furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/BioMap_CoreHabitatComponents/FeatureServer/2"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
aqua_core <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> mutate(layer = "aqua_core")

furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/BioMap_CoreHabitatComponents/FeatureServer/3"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
wetland <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> mutate(layer = "wetland")

furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/BioMap_CoreHabitatComponents/FeatureServer/4"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
rare_species <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> mutate(layer = "rare_species")

furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/BioMap_CoreHabitatComponents/FeatureServer/5"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
forest <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> mutate(layer = "forest")

furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/BioMap_CoreHabitatComponents/FeatureServer/6"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
vernal_pool <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> mutate(layer = "vernal_pool")
```

Join rows and fix geometries. Note that there are some pretty cool columns, 
specifically in the pncc, rare_species, and aqua_core datasets that I needed to 
drop to maintain consistent dat structure, but may be work looking into! You can 
read more about metadata [here](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/massgis-data-biomap-the-future-of-conservation)
```{r}

biomap <- pncc |> select(layer) |> 
  bind_rows(aqua_core)|> select(layer) |> 
   bind_rows(wetland)|> select(layer) |> 
   bind_rows(rare_species)|> select(layer) |> 
   bind_rows(forest)|> select(layer) |>
   bind_rows(vernal_pool)|> select(layer) |> 
  mutate(id = 1:18761) |> 
  st_make_valid()

rm(pncc, aqua_core, wetland, rare_species, forest, vernal_pool)
```

## Read in Protected Lands
I'm reading in the protected lands dataset and selecting the owner_type variable. 
One thing I noticed is that there are quite a few categories with less than (2000) observations (in total, they make up less than 10% of the data), so I'm going to call 
them "other" for now (Private Nonprofit, Public Nonprofit, Conservation Organization,
Other, Unknown, and County). 
```{r}
# read in and tidy
furl <- "https://arcgisserver.digital.mass.gov/arcgisserver/rest/services/AGOL/openspace/FeatureServer/0"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)
protect <- arc_select(flayer) |> clean_names() |> select(owner_type) |> 
  mutate(owner_type = case_when(
  owner_type == "N" ~ "Other",
  owner_type == "B" ~ "Other",
  owner_type == "G" ~ "Other",
  owner_type == "O" ~ "Other",
  owner_type == "X" ~ "Other",
  owner_type == "C" ~ "Other",
  .default = owner_type)) |> st_make_valid()

# dissolve polygons
biomap_diss <- biomap |>
  group_by(layer) |>
  summarize(geometry = st_union(geometry))

protect_diss <- protect |>
  group_by(owner_type) |>
  summarize(geometry = st_union(geometry))

# calculate acres of biomap area by group
biomap_denom <- biomap_diss |>
  mutate(biomap_acres = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 4046.856) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

# intersect with protected area polys and calculate areas
protected_by_owner <- st_intersection(biomap_diss, protect_diss) |>
  mutate(protected_acres = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 4046.856) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(layer, owner_type, protected_acres)

# biomap category by ownership type
tree_map_df <- protected_by_owner |>
  left_join(biomap_denom, by = "layer") |>
  mutate(pct_of_biomap = 100 * protected_acres/biomap_acres) |> 
  mutate(owner_type = case_when(
    owner_type == "F" ~ "Federal",
    owner_type == "L" ~ "Land Trust",
    owner_type == "M" ~ "Municipal",
    owner_type == "P" ~ "Private for Profit", 
    owner_type == "S" ~ "State", 
    .default = owner_type))

```

## Treemap 

This could probably made a bit prettier by formatting the legend.. 
```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8

tree_map_df |> 
ggplot(aes(
  area = protected_acres, fill = layer, label =  owner_type,
  subgroup = layer)) +
  geom_treemap(color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "white") +
  geom_treemap_text(
    colour = "black",
    reflow = T,
    place = "bottom",
    padding.x = grid::unit(1.5, "mm"),
    padding.y = grid::unit(2, "mm"), size = 20) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = soe_palette) +
  labs(fill = "BioMap Core Type")

## quick table 
tree_map_df |> 
  select(owner_type, layer, pct_of_biomap) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = "layer", values_from = "pct_of_biomap") |> 
  arrange(desc(forest)) |> 
  gt()
```



## Read in DCR Ecoregions
Data accessed from [MA DCR Feature Layer](https://wellesley.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=bce82aad47394bf7a3add219f3c92297#overview)
```{r}
furl <- "https://wellesley.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=bce82aad47394bf7a3add219f3c92297"
flayer <- arc_open(furl)

layer <- get_layer(flayer, 0)
ecoregions <- arc_select(layer)

# set CRS to match biomap data 
ecoregions <- ecoregions |> st_transform(st_crs(biomap_core_hab)) |> st_make_valid() |> 
  clean_names() |> select(econame)
```

# Calculate percent of Biomap Core Habitat per Ecoregion
```{r}
# total area
total_bio_area <- biomap_core_hab |>
  mutate(area = st_area(geometry)) |>
  pull(area) |>
  sum()

# prop area by ecoregion
bio_by_eco <- st_intersection(biomap_core_hab, ecoregions) |>
  mutate(area = st_area(geometry)) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(econame) |>
  summarise(area = sum(area)) |>
  mutate(perc_of_bio_area = (area / total_bio_area)*100)

## data distribution 
summary(bio_by_eco)
## cut data 
bio_by_eco <- bio_by_eco  |>
  mutate(perc_bio_cat = cut(perc_of_bio_area,
    breaks = c(1, 3.8, 6.6, 9.4, 23),
    labels = c("1-3.8%", "3.8-6.6%", "6.6-9.5%", "9.5-23%")))

bio_by_eco <- ecoregions |> left_join(bio_by_eco)

## map
bio_by_eco |>
  ggplot() + 
  geom_sf(aes(fill = perc_bio_cat)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(c("#DD5A54", "#EDBFB2", "#EC940C", "#608ED8")))
  
```
Note-- can likely afford to add correct font, remove background, and add legend 
and north arrow.
